headline: OpenPrinter launches: compact, open-source, repairable printer/plotter with independent ink
summary: This new printer/plotter supports both standard sheets and paper rolls for custom formats, eliminating frustrating ink blockages by allowing independent use of black and color cartridges.
details: OpenPrinter is a new printer/plotter designed to use black and color cartridges independently, ending the common frustration of being unable to print due to one empty color. It supports standard sheets and versatile paper rolls for banners, strips, and custom formats.

The device is built with standard and open-source components, making it easy to assemble, maintain, and repair. This design choice aims for longevity and helps reduce electronic waste by encouraging users to keep their machines and consumables longer.

Equipped with an open-source print server (CUPS), OpenPrinter offers a driver-free experience across Windows, MacOS, Linux, Android, and iOS. It handles both local and network printing for maximum flexibility.

OpenPrinter is designed to be the most compact printer/plotter on the market, fitting easily on a desk or mounted on a wall. Users can also personalize their printer by 3D printing custom parts, thanks to its open-source nature.

The cartridges are refillable and DRM-free, ensuring low ink and consumable costs. Open Tools will sell 'Inkit' refill kits, including four ink bottles and tools, with cartridges widely available in retail and online.

Beyond printing, OpenPrinter integrates with phone scanning apps like Genius Scan and CamScanner for high-definition document capture. This offers advantages over traditional scanners by leveraging existing smartphone capabilities.

The project is distributed under the Creative Commons BY-NC-SA 4.0 license, promoting free use, sharing, and modification for non-commercial purposes with proper attribution. This fosters collaboration and innovation within an ethical framework.

While embracing openness, Openprinter's technical architecture and design are protected by a patent and design registration. This ensures recognition of the design work while upholding the project's open-source spirit, with files to be shared once the final product is ready.
caption:

headline_marked: Flipper Zero [[recommits to firmware development]] and community contributions after user feedback
headline: Flipper Zero recommits to firmware development and community contributions after user feedback
summary: Flipper Devices will allocate resources to maintain Flipper Zero firmware, support community contributions, and implement new rules for feature requests and pull requests via GitHub Discussions.
details: Flipper Devices has announced a renewed commitment to Flipper Zero firmware development and community contributions, responding to strong user feedback. This decision rethinks their previous approach to project maintenance and community engagement.

The company will now allocate resources specifically for firmware maintenance and supporting community efforts. New guidelines include voting for feature requests in GitHub Discussions, clearer pull request guidelines, and mandatory integration testing.

When Flipper Zero launched on Kickstarter, the team faced immense pressure to deliver amidst skepticism and challenges like component shortages and political turmoil. They successfully navigated these hurdles, shipping the product despite accusations of being scammers.

A key technical limitation was the Flipper Zero's 700 KB flash memory, which quickly made it impossible to add new features directly. This led to the development of dynamic app loading from the microSD card, moving core functions into apps.

This architecture enabled the release of stable firmware 1.0 in 2024, alongside an Apps Catalog. The firmware API and SDK were stabilized for developers, reducing the need for frequent app rebuilds due to API changes.

Initially, Flipper Devices planned to limit official firmware work to critical bug fixes and infrastructure, shifting focus to new devices. They believed the existing community ecosystem of alternative firmware projects could drive further development.

However, the overwhelming community interest in official firmware development prompted a change of heart. With over a million users, direct communication became unmanageable, making it hard to discern genuine community needs from individual requests.

To address this, all community requests will now be centralized on GitHub Discussions. This platform will allow users to vote on feature requests, helping the Flipper Zero team prioritize and integrate the most impactful contributions.
caption:
Flipper Zero is changing its approach to firmware development and community contributions. The company is re-engaging with its user base to prioritize features.
